request: One Gemini-generated visual overview in each part introduction, connecting every chapter to the part's overall theme.

illustrations.visual_goal: Map six financial-foundation chapters into three connected stages, culminating in money and terms a company commitment can rely on.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "UNDERSTAND".
Six chapter cards, arranged as three wide rows with two cards per row. A restrained label above each row identifies the stage. Read the cards left to right inside each row, then proceed down to the next row. Use clear teal arrows within each row and connecting the row groups vertically; all connections must avoid text. A single gold purpose banner spans the bottom.

Top row stage label: "Trace money and control".
Left card title: "Customers, lenders, investors"; subtitle: "What each source expects". Small ledger and coins symbol.
Right card title: "Funding and control"; subtitle: "Who receives and authorizes cash". Small cash-routing or approval symbol.
Arrow left to right.

Middle row stage label: "Interpret value and expectations".
Left card title: "Valuation"; subtitle: "Numbers and assumptions". Small magnifying glass over figures.
Right card title: "Investor returns"; subtitle: "Same performance, different outcomes". Small branching return paths.
Arrow left to right.

Bottom row stage label: "Confirm funding for the work".
Left card title: "Funding choices"; subtitle: "Match the money to the work". Small fitted funding block.
Right card title: "Cash flow"; subtitle: "Available cash and dates". Small calendar and coins.
Arrow left to right.

The three rows connect top to middle to bottom. An arrow from the bottom row leads to the gold banner. Banner exact text: "Know what can fund a commitment".
Exactly six chapter cards, every title appears once. The outcome is conditional on actual funding and terms, not automatic financing.
illustrations.alt: Six chapters build through three stages: customers, lenders and investors lead to funding and control; valuation leads to investor returns; funding choices lead to cash flow. Together they establish what can fund a commitment.
illustrations.caption: The six chapters build from the sources and control of money, through valuation and returns, to a funding choice checked against available cash. Short labels correspond to the linked chapters below.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Connect authority, incentives and investor fit to accountable decisions, with a feedback path when evidence under pressure changes the arrangements.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "ALIGN".
Three large chapter cards form a left-to-right sequence across the upper-middle of the image. Each has a concise two-line subtitle and a small editorial symbol. Large clear teal arrows connect card 1 to card 2 to card 3. A fine curved return arrow runs above the cards from card 3 back to card 1, with the exact short label "Revisit the arrangements". Leave enough whitespace that the return arrow and label do not touch the main heading.

Left card title: "Clarify authority"; subtitle: "Who can decide and deliver?" Symbol: signed decision sheet.
Middle card title: "Compare incentives and stakes"; subtitle: "What does each party gain or risk?" Symbol: balance with different stakes.
Right card title: "Assess investor fit"; subtitle: "How does the relationship handle pressure?" Symbol: agreement or bridge being tested.

Below the cards, three fine connectors converge into one wide ochre purpose banner, making clear all three chapters contribute. Banner exact text: "Accountable decisions with competing demands explicit".
Exactly three chapter cards. Do not imply shared ownership automatically aligns interests. The return arrow means observed behavior can reopen decision and escalation arrangements.
illustrations.alt: Authority establishes who decides; incentives reveal what each party gains or risks; investor fit tests behavior under pressure. All three support accountable decisions, with a return arrow to revisit the arrangements.
illustrations.caption: Authority establishes who decides; incentives explain the competing stakes; investor fit tests the working relationship. Evidence under pressure can send you back to the decision arrangements.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Show nine chapters in three connected moves: choose and justify work; assess and change delivery; apply the common method to four operating choices.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "COMMIT".
Exactly NINE chapter cards organized into THREE clearly separated horizontal bands, stacked from top to bottom. Make labels large enough to read; keep symbols very small or omit them if they compete with text. This is a compact overview, not a tall poster.

First band label: "Choose and justify the work".
Two chapter cards across the band, with an arrow between them:
"Set priorities" / "Fit cash and capacity"
"Test revenue assumptions" / "Trace customer benefit"

A centered downward arrow connects the first band to the second.
Second band label: "Assess and change delivery".
Three chapter cards across the band, with arrows left to right:
"Assess capability" / "Find the constraint"
"Trace the work" / "Fix roles and decisions"
"Plan for growth" / "Choose system changes"

A centered downward arrow connects the second band to the third.
Third band label: "Apply the same reasoning".
Four chapter cards in a clearly balanced TWO-BY-TWO grid within this band. Top-left "Cloud costs" / "Test the service unit"; top-right "Resilience" / "Correct and retest"; bottom-left "AI strategy" / "Separate three questions"; bottom-right "Acquisitions and separations" / "Fund transition work".
These four application cards have NO arrows between them: they are different applications of the shared method, not sequential prerequisites. Use a single branch or bracket to show that the same reasoning reaches all four.

An arrow from the third band reaches one gold bottom banner: "Fund feasible work and review the evidence".
Only the listed nine chapter cards; no extra or duplicated card. Do not number chapters or suggest that cloud changes must precede resilience, AI or acquisitions.
illustrations.alt: Nine chapters form three moves: priorities and revenue assumptions justify the work; capability, work organization and system design establish delivery; cloud, resilience, AI and acquisitions or separations apply the same reasoning. The shared outcome is feasible funded work reviewed against evidence.
illustrations.caption: The first five chapters establish what deserves investment and what delivery requires. The final four apply that reasoning to different choices; their grouping shows a shared method rather than a dependency between applications.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Connect working arrangements, the source of help and engagement terms to the adviser and operating partner roles, culminating in useful support with explicit accountability.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "COLLABORATE".
Exactly FIVE chapter cards in a coherent two-level framework, flowing downward to a gold purpose banner.
Top level has three chapter cards across, connected left to right:
"Plan investor support" / "Match the arrangement to priorities" (small paired organization blocks)
"Choose the right help" / "Compare sources for the gap" (small choice or search symbol)
"Set the terms of help" / "Agree work, authority and handover" (small agreement sheet)

The top sequence leads into a second level with two larger cards side by side, grouped under the exact label "Understand the people behind the help":
"Clarify the adviser's role" / "Assignment and reporting relationship" (small single specialist symbol)
"Technology operating partners" / "Wider support for the company" (small connected capability nodes)
Treat these two as complementary lenses, without implying that an adviser must become an operating partner, or that every company needs both. Show a branch from the agreed-support framework to both role cards. No arrow from one role card to the other.

Both role cards connect to the single ochre bottom purpose banner. Banner exact text: "Useful support with accountability, cost and dependence understood".
The visual should read as overall arrangement, chosen help, agreed engagement, then the people and function supporting it. No investor superiority claim and no assumed mandatory investor intervention.
illustrations.alt: The working arrangement leads to a choice of help and agreed engagement terms. The adviser and technology operating partner chapters clarify the people and wider function behind that help. Together they support useful collaboration with accountability, cost and dependence understood.
illustrations.caption: The working arrangement shapes the help you seek and the terms you agree. The last two chapters clarify the individual adviser and the wider operating function, so support contributes to a company plan with clear accountability.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Keep the evidence-carrying onboarding scenario separate from the delayed-financing scenario and its conditional reduction, while connecting both to leadership through change.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "LEAD".
Exactly FIVE chapter cards arranged in TWO distinct vertical lanes with generous separation, converging only on a shared ochre purpose banner at the bottom. Make the separation explicit: these are two different fictional scenarios, not one mandatory ownership timeline.

Left lane heading: "Follow the onboarding finding".
Three cards stacked with downward arrows:
"Use diligence" / "Record what changes the plan"
"Plan the first hundred days" / "Fund work and review the finding"
"Manage the handover" / "Carry evidence and obligations"
A thin continuous teal line or file symbol may emphasize the same finding travels through these three chapters.

Right lane heading: "Separate funding-delay scenario".
Two cards stacked:
"Manage funding delays" / "Revise cash and commitments"
"Plan layoffs" / "Decide what work stops"
The only arrow between these cards must be dashed and labelled EXACTLY "If a reduction is required". This is conditional: a delayed financing does not inevitably mean layoffs. Position the condition text in a clear gap between the cards.

There must be NO arrows between the two lanes. Each lane has a downward connector into the shared gold bottom banner. Banner exact text: "Keep decisions, evidence and obligations accountable through change".
Use small document, calendar or handover icons, not distressed people. No automatic buyout-to-exit timeline. Exactly three chapter cards in the left lane and two in the right; do not duplicate handover in the right lane.
illustrations.alt: One path carries the onboarding finding from diligence to a funded first-hundred-days plan and handover. A separate path revises commitments when financing is delayed and proceeds to layoffs only if a reduction is required. Both support accountable leadership through change.
illustrations.caption: One scenario carries a finding from diligence into a funded plan and its handover. A separate funding-delay scenario may require a reduction. Both develop ways to lead through change; events have no mandatory order.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Bring four independent case chapters through a common reading method into the closing chapter's test of durable success.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "LEARN".
Exactly FIVE chapter cards. Four case-study cards form a two-by-two grid in the upper portion, under the small group label "Four independent case chapters":
Top-left: "Hilton and Skype" / "Explain the successful exit"
Top-right: "Visma" / "Check continuity of money"
Bottom-left: "Toys R Us" / "Test the cash behind earnings"
Bottom-right: "TeamSystem" / "Trace inherited obligations"
Use small open-book or evidence symbols, not corporate logos. NO arrows between the four case cards: these histories do not cause one another.

The four cards feed, using clear converging connectors, into one narrow unboxed reading-method line below the grid. Exact line: "Evidence → possible mechanism → leadership decision". Make the line fully readable, split across two lines only if needed.
A downward arrow leads from this common method into the fifth chapter card, centered and wide: "Success for whom, and for how long?" / "Compare gains, costs and continuing capability".
One arrow leads from this fifth card to a gold purpose banner. Banner exact text: "Make judgments the evidence supports".
Do not add historical dates, financial results, causal claims or another case. The four independent case chapters contribute different tests to the fifth chapter's synthesis; preserve that distinction.
illustrations.alt: Four independent case chapters—Hilton and Skype, Visma, Toys R Us and TeamSystem—feed an evidence-to-mechanism-to-decision method. Their lessons reach the closing chapter, Success for Whom and for How Long, which compares gains, costs and continuing capability.
illustrations.caption: Four independent case chapters feed a shared reading method and the closing chapter's test of durable success. The case table below keeps each lesson within its historical window.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough
